meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.
It was an interesting movie, right?
Well yes, bye.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mom' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давай за мою маму и за ее мудрые советы.
examples.trans: Let's drink to my mom and her wise advice.
Yes, Mom, I am not at home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.

examples.text: И не будет у меня звезды.
examples.trans: And I will not have a star.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И не будет у меня звезды.
examples.trans: And I will not have a star.

examples.text: Не знаю, я на экран не смотрел особо.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not really look at the screen.
They offered me a new job.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'at home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maybe I really should quit this madhouse?

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'called in', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.trans: They called me in to work, an urgent banquet.
You called a sober driver!
We immediately called an ambulance.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не знаю, я на экран не смотрел особо.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not really look at the screen.
I have very important news.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I agree to work for you.
They offered me a new job.
Sorry, a new job?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('urgent').

examples.trans: And we need to answer urgently.
They called me in to work, an urgent banquet.
I need an urgent call.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'banquet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They called me in to work, an urgent banquet.

examples.text: У нас сегодня очень важный банкет.
examples.trans: We have a very important banquet today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пожалела себя, я тебя уволю, а у меня Катя весь мозг съест.
examples.trans: I felt sorry for myself, if I fire you Katya will nag me to death.
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well yes, bye.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, shall I go?
Well yes, bye.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это замечательно, ты будешь первым поваром России.
examples.trans: That is wonderful, you will be the first chef in Russia.
And you wrote a culinary book.

examples.text: Рассчитали, от трех до пяти тысяч за блюдо.
examples.trans: We calculated them, from three to five thousand per dish.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ready').

examples.text: Шеф, мы можем ребрышки из старого меню приготовить?
examples.trans: Chef, can we prepare ribs from the old menu?
We will prepare everything right now!
I understood everything, I am ready.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to skate / ride'.

examples.trans: Well, are you ready to skate?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и кататься вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to skate on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maybe I really should quit this madhouse?

examples.text: Это замечательно, ты будешь первым поваром России.

оказываться.gloss: to turn out to be, prove to be

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be, find oneself
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, prove to be', paired with 'оказаться'.

examples.trans: Simple things turn out to be important.

examples.text: Иногда простые вещи оказываются самыми важными.
examples.trans: Sometimes simple things turn out to be the most important.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ложный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('harder / more complicated').

examples.text: Это оказывается сложнее, чем я думал.
examples.trans: This turns out to be harder than I thought.
Look, there's nothing complicated.
That's a very difficult question.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'than', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф, а почему блюда такие маленькие?
examples.trans: Chef, why are the dishes so tiny?
And why is it so expensive?

examples.text: Это оказывается сложнее, чем я думал.
examples.trans: This turns out to be harder than I thought.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'thought', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.text: Ну что, думаешь, пора уже с Катей поговорить?
examples.trans: Well, do you think it is time to talk to Katya already?

examples.text: Это оказывается сложнее, чем я думал.
examples.trans: This turns out to be harder than I thought.
I'm thinking about work.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is the staff meeting about anyway?

examples.text: Я же не знаю, как у вас принято за девушками ухаживать.

examples.text: Сегодня в вашей жизни историческое событие.

meanings.en: to turn out well, to succeed, to manage (impersonal + dative)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'даться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to succeed, to manage', paired with 'удаваться'.

examples.trans: How did you manage that?

examples.text: Я не поняла, как тебе это удалось.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.

examples.trans: Yes, and where is the wine?

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guests' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And where are all the guests?
All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'хмелье'). Common neuter noun meaning 'hangover' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Is there nobody to work because of a hangover?

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть похмелье.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.trans: I agree to work for you.

examples.text: Я не понял, она у нас работает?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'кого').

examples.trans: Is there nobody to work because of a hangover?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There is no old menu, there is only the new menu.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Извините, но я решил остаться в ресторане.
examples.trans: Forgive me, but I decided to stay at the restaurant.
We are changing the restaurant's concept.
This is a restaurant of auteur cuisine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.text: Нет, ресторан закрыли, шефа будут снимать.
examples.trans: No, they closed the restaurant, they are going to film the chef.

examples.text: Я не поняла, почему ресторан закрыт?
examples.trans: I do not understand, why is the restaurant closed?
They even closed the restaurant for us.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.text: Сегодня в вашей жизни историческое событие.
examples.trans: Today is a historic event in your lives.
Tonight we will celebrate the event.

examples.text: Я-то вам зачем, вам надо побыть наедине.
examples.trans: Why do you need me, you two need to be alone together.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take off, peel', paired with 'снять'.

examples.text: И теперь будем снимать в реальных ресторанах.
examples.trans: And now we will film in real restaurants.
They want to film right here at our place!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are changing the restaurant's concept.

examples.text: Может, мы пока старое меню оставим?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'обрать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take away (by force), confiscate', paired with 'отбирать'.

examples.text: Мы вот овощи отобрали самые красивые.
examples.trans: We selected the most beautiful vegetables here.
We'll take the TVs away!
Oh sure, right now they'll take them away!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most').

examples.trans: Decide for yourself.

examples.text: Давай выпьем за наших девушек, они у нас самые лучшие.
examples.trans: Let's drink to our girls, they are the very best.

examples.text: Мы вот овощи отобрали самые красивые.
examples.trans: We selected the most beautiful vegetables here.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful').

examples.text: Мы вот овощи отобрали самые красивые.
examples.trans: We selected the most beautiful vegetables here.

examples.text: Нет, ты самая красивая девушка на свете.
examples.trans: No, you are the most beautiful girl in the world.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: А я выпью, у тебя это очень хорошо получается.
examples.trans: Well I will drink, you are very good at that.

Alright, got it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Я не знаю, я ничего не понял.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not understand anything.

examples.text: Он сказал, что половину слов в меню не понял.
examples.trans: He said that he did not understand half the words on the menu.

examples.text: Я не понял, она у нас работает?
examples.trans: I do not understand, does she work here with us?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: I am very tired today.

examples.text: Сегодня в вашей жизни историческое событие.
examples.trans: Today is a historic event in your lives.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером все выпьют и расслабятся.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дача'). Common feminine noun meaning 'broadcast' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Today we are filming a show!

examples.text: Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.
